title: Check yourself: the kinds of method reference

questions.stem: An upload filter holds `BiFunction<String, String, Boolean> check = String::endsWith;` and calls `check.apply("ledger-q3.csv", ".csv")`. What is the result?

options.text: It returns false, since the second argument is the object endsWith runs on and the first is its parameter
options.says: the receiver of an unbound reference is the first parameter, not the last

options.text: It returns true, since the first argument is the object endsWith runs on and the second is its parameter
options.says: an unbound reference makes the interface's first parameter the receiver and passes the rest to the method

options.text: It does not compile, since endsWith has one parameter and the BiFunction passes it two
options.says: an unbound reference needs one interface parameter more than the method has, for the receiver

options.text: It does not compile, since endsWith is an instance method and String::endsWith gives it no object
options.says: Class::instanceMethod is an unbound reference: the object comes from the interface's first argument

origin.section: `Class::method` Is Static or Unbound, and the Method's Declaration Decides Which

questions.stem: `Double` declares both `static String toString(double)` and `String toString()`. A report column is declared as `Function<Double, String> cell = Double::toString;` and later used as `cell.apply(2.5)`. What happens?

options.text: It prints 2.5, since javac prefers the instance toString() when the argument can be the object
options.says: javac prefers neither: when the static and the unbound search both find a method, the reference is ambiguous

options.text: It prints 2.5, since javac prefers the static toString(double) when the argument can be unboxed
options.says: javac prefers neither: when the static and the unbound search both find a method, the reference is ambiguous

options.text: It does not compile, since javac finds both toString(double) and toString() and picks neither
options.says: Double has a static toString(double) and an instance toString(); both fit, so javac reports the reference as ambiguous

options.text: It does not compile, since javac finds toString(double) but cannot unbox the Double to call it
options.says: the argument is unboxed for the static method, as Integer is for toString(int); that is why both fit and the reference is ambiguous

origin.section: `Class::method` Is Static or Unbound, and the Method's Declaration Decides Which

questions.stem: Given `record Badge(String holder, int level) {}`, an audit log holds `Function<Object, String> show = Object::toString;` and logs `show.apply(new Badge("Jane Doe", 2))`. What is logged?

options.text: Badge[holder=Jane Doe, level=2], since the class of the object passed in decides which toString runs
options.says: an unbound reference is a virtual call: the receiver's own toString, the record's, runs

options.text: Badge@ and a hash code, since the class written before :: decides which toString runs
options.says: the class before :: decides what compiles, not which body runs; the call is virtual

options.text: Nothing, since the line does not compile: an unbound reference must name the object's own class
options.says: an unbound reference may name a superclass or interface of the receiver, such as Object or CharSequence

options.text: Nothing, since the line does not compile: toString takes no parameter and the Function passes one
options.says: the Function's one parameter becomes the receiver of the parameterless toString

origin.section: Through a Supertype, the Call Still Reaches the Override

questions.stem: A job router keeps `Map<Integer, List<Integer>> queues = new HashMap<>();` keyed by port, and runs `queues.computeIfAbsent(8080, ArrayList::new).add(17);` on an empty map. What does `queues.get(8080)` print?

options.text: Nothing, since the line does not compile: computeIfAbsent needs a Function and ArrayList::new is a Supplier
options.says: a constructor reference has no shape of its own; the target type picks a constructor that fits a Function

options.text: Nothing, since the line does not compile: no ArrayList constructor takes the Integer key
options.says: the Integer key is unboxed for ArrayList(int initialCapacity), so the line compiles

options.text: [8080, 17], since the key is passed to the new list's constructor as its first element
options.says: no ArrayList constructor takes an element; an Integer key selects ArrayList(int initialCapacity)

options.text: [17], since the key is passed to the new list's constructor as its initial capacity
options.says: computeIfAbsent calls its Function with the key, so ArrayList::new resolves to ArrayList(int initialCapacity)

origin.section: `Class::new` Picks Its Constructor From the Interface's Parameters
